title.narrative: Emergency Food Intervention – Malakal Town, Upper Nile State

description.narrative: In August and September 2022, fighting and displacement has occurred in Upper Nile state, leading to the displacement of many thousands of people. The Head of UNMISS in South Sudan says “fighting between Sudan People's Liberation Movement/Army-In Opposition (SPLM-IO) forces and the Kitgwang and Agwelek factions has displaced thousands of people within Upper Nile, to Jonglei, Unity states, and parts of Sudan," with some 14,000 people displaced into Malakal POC site. In relation to the programming areas of Caritas Diocese of Malakal (CDOM) and CAFOD and Trócaire in Partnership (CTP) programming: initial conflict broke out between members of the Kitgwang and Agwelek forces on the outskirts of Tonga in Panyikang County in early August. The fighting spread into Tonga Town, and to Nyiluak and surrounding villages, displacing many civilians. Those forced to leave their homes faced harsh conditions, unable to carry food or belongings, crossing long distances and flooded areas. Some children and older people were drowned. An estimated 27,000 people were displaced due to this fighting, and settled in Pakang Payam. CDOM colleagues and Bishop Stephen Nyodho of the Diocese of Malakal visited Adidihang on 30th August, one of the two major sites where displaced people were settled (details of this IRNA are below). The situation continued to deteriorate into September. On 5th September, some security incidents occurred in Malakal town. A demonstration against some administrative decisions taken by the State Government turned violent, and gun fire was exchanged. One person was confirmed killed. On 7th September, the recently established Adhidhang IDPs camp in Malakal County was attacked and raided by armed elements, leaving an unconfirmed number of casualties and a very high number of wounded. More than 100 reached treatment facilities at the UN Protection of Civilians site near Malakal. The number of people killed as not been ascertained, but it is suspected to be more than 30. The attack was condemned by UNMISS. Thousands left the area, destined for Malakal Town.
